thingsToDo.title: Fort Myers River District
thingsToDo.description: Walk the historic downtown for early-20th-century architecture, galleries, restaurants, public art, and Caloosahatchee River views.

thingsToDo.title: Edison and Ford Winter Estates
thingsToDo.description: Tour the historic homes, gardens, museum, and laboratory associated with Thomas Edison and Henry Ford.

thingsToDo.title: Six Mile Cypress Slough Preserve
thingsToDo.description: Use the boardwalk through wetland habitat for birding, wildlife, and a close look at Southwest Florida's freshwater ecology.

thingsToDo.title: Manatee Park
thingsToDo.description: Visit this county park on the Orange River for seasonal manatee viewing opportunities, especially when Gulf waters cool.

thingsToDo.title: Caloosahatchee River
thingsToDo.description: Use riverfront walks or boating to understand the waterway that shaped Fort Myers' location and development.

thingsToDo.title: Fort Myers Beach and Sanibel — separate destinations
thingsToDo.description: Plan Gulf beach time as a separate excursion; neither Fort Myers Beach nor Sanibel is part of the City of Fort Myers.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Cooler months are easiest for outdoor planning
bullets: Late fall through early spring generally brings lower humidity and comfortable outdoor conditions.
Summer is hot, humid, and storm-prone; start exposed activities early and keep afternoon plans flexible.
Busy winter and holiday periods reward advance reservations for popular tours and timed attractions.

travelTips: Group each day by geography instead of crossing the region repeatedly.
Use early mornings for exposed outdoor activities and waterfront time.
Check park, marine, and weather conditions before nature-focused plans.
Treat nearby municipalities and protected areas as separate destinations with their own access rules.

faq.q: How many days should I plan for Fort Myers?
faq.a: Two to three days is a good starting point for the core sights plus one outdoor or regional experience.

faq.q: Is Fort Myers good for outdoor travelers?
faq.a: Yes. The strongest itineraries combine the destination itself with nearby water, parks, preserves, or trails.
It depends on the destination, but a car or guided tour is often useful for protected lands and regional excursions.

faq.q: Should I book tours in advance?
faq.a: For high-demand wildlife, boating, park, and holiday-period experiences, advance booking is sensible.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Fort Myers is an incorporated mainland city on the Caloosahatchee River.

sections.heading: Geography & setting
paragraphs: The river links the city to estuaries and Gulf islands farther west, while inland wetlands shape the local ecology.

sections.heading: History & culture
paragraphs: The River District and Edison/Ford legacy provide historical depth beyond the region's beach image.

sections.heading: Outdoor & seasonal highlights
paragraphs: Wetland preserves, river boating, birding, and seasonal wildlife viewing are the main outdoor complements.

sections.heading: Getting around
paragraphs: Downtown is walkable, but preserves and Gulf islands require a car or tour and should be grouped geographically.
